quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. The rear wheel should touch the curb.

questions.question: What is most important for an eye or face shield to be effective?

options.text: Prevent all air from passing through.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely to your head. It should be scratch-free, protect your eyes from impact, let you see to the sides, allow air to flow (to prevent fogging), and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Stay in the center part of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center part of your lane. Getting closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What does a left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a hand signal. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When should a passenger mount a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: A passenger should board the motorcycle only after the engine starts and is in neutral. The passenger should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with the rider's control. The passenger should hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should a group of three-wheel motorcycles travel together?
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles travel best in a staggered formation. However, three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this formation. They should travel in a single-file line instead.

questions.question: The middle of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually provides enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is narrow, so you can ride to the side of it and still be in the center of the lane. Avoid it when the road is wet.

questions.question: Should you wear a riding jacket in hot weather?

options.text: Yes, it can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat problems.
Only if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from injury and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: What is true about the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle.
It has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. Avoid areas with heavy buildup of oil and grease, usually found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: When the road is wet, what part of the lane should you avoid?
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this usually provides enough grip. When wet, avoid it. The oily strip is narrow enough that you can ride to the side and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Staying in the center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on either side of the lane can cause a crash with the passing vehicle or encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When you can see through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when you need more time to stop, such as in heavy traffic, poor weather, at night, or when you cannot see ahead clearly.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles lean to turn. To make the motorcycle lean in the direction you want to turn, press the handgrip on that side.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in snow, rain, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without one.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week as part of your pre-ride inspection to ensure safe riding.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure smoothly and gradually for better control.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. These signs tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Always stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both vehicles are stopped. The other vehicle might back up without warning. You also need space to move away if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. Squeeze the front brake harder as you slow down and ease off the rear brake. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Abruptly apply both brakes while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you need to stop quickly while turning, straighten the motorcycle first and square the handlebars, then brake. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes gently and gradually while reducing your lean, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: As an operator, you should prepare a passenger to ride by instructing them to do each of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, your passenger should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist or belt. They should keep their legs away from the hot muffler, chains, and other moving parts.
